clue.text: Like the Sabbath day, happening in silence

blocks.note: the hushing sound used to call for quiet
a happening is an event

explanation.surface: A description of the Sabbath as a day passed in quiet observance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Happening in silence' reads as a description of the day; it is wordplay, one piece placed inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis the Sabbath is the seventh day of the week, the day of rest.

clue.text: Annie Oakley's heavenly body

second meaning: a meteor streaking across the night sky

explanation.walkthrough: Annie Oakley was the famous sharpshooter of Buffalo Bill's Wild West show, so she was literally a star at shooting.
explanation.definitionFit: A meteor is popularly called a shooting star, and the phrase also fits a celebrated marksman.

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

clue.text: Inn's peppery seasoning lacking a bit of thyme

the first letter of thyme

clue.text: Representative sample of small timepiece

the postal abbreviation for Iowa

clue.text: Four-minute mile, four-minute mile, four-minute mile…

explanation.walkthrough: Roger Bannister's sub-four-minute mile smashed a record, and endlessly repeating the same thing is like a scratched vinyl disc skipping.

clue.text: Conductor to read in Icelandic, initially

taken as written
the first letter of Icelandic

clue.text: Tears apart flower

blocks.note: taken as written

clue.text: Horribly evil curse and foul vice lures private into warped, cruel vise

explanation.surface: A villain's lurid scheme of curses and vices dragging someone into a torture device.
explanation.walkthrough: A setters' joke: 'foul vice lures' and 'warped, cruel vise' are two more anagrams of the same nine letters, so the answer can be built three ways around 'private'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone reclusive keeps to themselves, avoiding company, so the word is a synonym for private.

clue.text: Nouveaux riches from an average planet
